phaseA.result: Fast CI restored; timing breakdown and isolation audit recorded. No browser coverage removed or skipped.

phaseB.warmResult: 56/56 passed; cache hit; browser-tests job about 48s; full workflow about 67s.
phaseB.result: Pinned ubuntu-24.04 plus versioned Playwright Chromium cache reduced warm browser-test job latency by about 28% and full workflow latency by about 26%, with no coverage, worker-count, storage-growth, or production/runtime behavior reduction.
phaseB.rca: The first experiment exposed a pre-existing viewer-live-refresh synchronization race; the test now waits for semantic refresh completion instead of assuming an updated table means the whole refresh finished.

phaseC.result: Two workers reduced the warm full-suite Playwright time by about one third and browser-job time by about 19% versus the accepted workers=1 Phase B baseline, with all 56 tests and storage-growth coverage unchanged.

codeBaseline.note: Stage 19 final browser/test state is fully Chromium-verified. The one-time push trigger used to start Browser CI was removed immediately afterward; no temporary CI scaffolding remains.

stage19.result: Real Leumi provider collection, persistence, Viewer behavior and long-run stability were evidenced; repeated launch may open another Viewer but must not duplicate the Recorder.

contextArchitecture.result: Fresh-chat HOT context is bounded and preserved history is discoverable. Repository self-maintenance guards now enforce the structure during future changes.
